surfaceMeaning: Standard grid on a source-informed shape model; no resolved global surface map.
name: Achlys
credit: Dias-Oliveira et al. (2017), AJ 154, 22; four stellar occultations
shapeMeaning: Published Jacobi-ellipsoid interpretation, with semiaxes 470 ±20, 383 ±10 and 245 ±8 km. It assumes hydrostatic equilibrium and a 6.75-hour rotation; the smooth shape is inferred from occultations, not imaged terrain.
orientationMeaning: Illustrative pole RA 0°, declination 90° and arbitrary meridian. The paper’s local projected-limb and opening angles do not provide a unique absolute surface attitude for this display.
periodText: About 6.75 hours in the adopted shape interpretation; display phase is illustrative
introduction: Formerly 2003 AZ84, Achlys is a plutino in Neptune’s 3: 2 orbital resonance. Its changing occultation silhouette supports a flattened, elongated model, while a grazing event hints at a local depression.

numericEvidence.section: Dias-Oliveira et al. (2017), section IV.2 and conclusions
numericEvidence.radiusFormula: cbrt(470 * 383 * 245); volume-equivalent model radius, not the paper’s projected area-equivalent radius 386 ±6 km
modelAssumptions: Single-peaked 6.75-hour modulation attributed to albedo variation
Fixed pole between 2012 and 2014 within limited aspect changes
numericEvidence.namingReference: WGSBN Bulletin 5(15), 2025 June 30, page 16: (208996) Achlys = 2003 AZ84

unresolved: The hydrostatic-equilibrium interpretation is conditional; no precise absolute spin attitude is supplied.
A limb depression admits several profiles; it is not reproduced as fabricated global topography.
The small satellite is outside this primary-body package.
